transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-03
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Markus (Redwood SE), Arjun (Redwood SE), Priya (Head of ML - Asterion), Samir (Infra), Carla (CTO), Luis (Security)

---
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. we'll give a quick agenda: kickoff, line up gates for access, agree success criteria and milestones, and then blockers. sorry if i talk fast, timezone juggling.
[00:18] Priya Nandan: Hey Lena, thanks. quick context: we're trying to replace our legacy reranker and augment generation in our triage flow. main asks are latency under 200ms p50 for single-turn, cost below our current baseline, and high intent accuracy on our internal data.
[00:35] Markus Chen: cool, thanks. to make sure we're aligned, when you say latency 200ms p50, is that end-to-end including network and our proxy, or just inference?
[00:45] Priya Nandan: good question. end-to-end from our app to response. so we need to include network. for the POC we can instrument 2 measurements: pure inference and app e2e.
[00:58] Samir Patel: on infra side, we run in GCP with private VPCs and strict egress. we'll need VPC peering / Private Service Connect or a gateway — depends on what you support. we also want to avoid exploding our whitelists.
[01:15] Lena Ortiz: Redwood Private supports VPC peering and a private control plane option; for hosted we usually do an outbound TLS with allowed IPs, but for enterprise we can do VPC peering. we'll add the network checklist to the runbook.
[01:30] Carla Hughes: timeline? we have an exec offsite mid-July and want a readout then. realistic?
[01:38] Arjun Rao: If we start now, a 6-week POC with a checkpoint at week 3 mid-point review and an exec readout in week 6 is realistic. week 1 kickoff & access, week 2 infra + sample workload upload, week 3 baseline benchmarks, week 4 optimization (batching/quant), week 5 scale runs, week 6 readout.
[01:58] Priya Nandan: sounds good, as long as we get early numbers by week 3.
[02:05] Markus Chen: for the benchmarks, we propose measuring: p50/p95 latency (inference-only and e2e), tokens/sec throughput at target prompt lengths, replication of QA/intent accuracy (top1/top3), and cost per 1k tokens / cost per request. we'll provide a benchmark spreadsheet where you'll fill observed metrics.
[02:25] Priya Nandan: can you suggest target model families? we prefer open weights but also want predictable perf.
[02:33] Markus Chen: we'll propose 2 model variants: a higher-accuracy 7B float model and a quantized 4-bit variant for cost comparisons. also include a 3rd fallback—smaller 3B—if latency requirements are strict. note that quantization may slightly affect accuracy; we'll measure deltas on your eval set.
[02:55] Luis Moreno: security: SOC 2 + ISO are table stakes. we need KMS integration and audit logs for all calls. also data retention rules — we can't have customer data persisted outside our region for regulated PHI workloads.
[03:12] Lena Ortiz: understood. Redwood supports KMS/HSM integrations and can enable region-locked storage for logs. we'll attach our compliance pack and a short checklist. also we can provision shorter log retention for the POC.
[03:30] Samir Patel: on sizing: our peak QPS for this flow is about 120 QPS, but it's spiky. for the POC we can run synthetic traffic at 50 QPS sustained and a 250 QPS spike. what's Redwood's recommended GPU footprint for the 7B and 4-bit options?
[03:48] Markus Chen: rough estimates: 7B float single-instance throughput around 60-80 tokens/sec on an A100-class instance; quantized 4-bit can double that in some cases. for 50 QPS with 40 tokens avg that's ~2k tokens/sec steady — we'd recommend 2 dedicated workers with autoscaling to handle spikes. we'll put exact sizing in the runbook after we see your token length distribution.
[04:12] Priya Nandan: ok that's helpful. also we need to measure tokenization mismatch — ours uses a slightly different tokenizer for clinical notes and sometimes tokens are longer.
[04:23] Arjun Rao: we'll ask you to provide a corpus sample so we can run tokenization and measure average tokens per prompt; that's in the benchmark template.
[04:32] Priya Nandan: on success criteria, triage team wants top-1 intent accuracy >= 88% compared to current on-prem model, latency p50 e2e < 250ms, and cost improvement >= 20% or at least parity while improving accuracy.
[04:48] Lena Ortiz: great. we'll capture that as POC success gates: 1) accuracy >= 88% on your eval set, 2) e2e latency p50 < 250ms under target load, 3) cost per 1k tokens <= your baseline or clear optimization path documented.
[05:00] Carla Hughes: executive readout should include a risk register — dependencies, compliance gaps, and any long lead-time items.
[05:07] Lena Ortiz: yes we'll include a short risk register in the runbook.
[05:12] Priya Nandan: what about model rollouts and A/B testing for this POC? we want a small internal canary before exec readout.
[05:20] Markus Chen: we can do a canary with 5-10% traffic to the new model variants and have an automatic fallback to current model for errors. Redwood's rollout feature supports canary and automatic rollback thresholds. we'll include a sample rollout config in the runbook.
[05:36] Luis Moreno: audit trail — we need to show who invoked model endpoints in the readout. is that exportable?
[05:41] Arjun Rao: yes, parameter-level audit logs with user IDs and timestamps are exportable. we'll show a sample log format.
[05:48] Priya Nandan: any blockers from Redwood side?
[05:51] Lena Ortiz: main blockers are: 1) getting your sample workloads and traffic profile, 2) VPC peering and service account, and 3) security sign-off on KMS integration. once those are in place we can run week 3 baseline benchmarks.
[06:07] Samir Patel: will need to check with our network team about peering windows — may take 3-5 business days.
[06:12] Lena Ortiz: understood. we'll set the kickoff access checklist as an action item.
[06:17] Markus Chen: quick note about benchmarking methodology: we prefer to run both synthetic load (to validate throughput and latency) and replay your real traffic on a sandbox to validate quality metrics. synthetic runs are deterministic, replays reveal noise from tokenization and prompt shaping.
[06:34] Priya Nandan: ok we'll prioritize a 10k-sample set for replay.
[06:38] Carla Hughes: who will present the exec readout?
[06:41] Lena Ortiz: usually our AE presents outcomes and the SE covers the technical deep dive. we'll prep a 15-20 minute deck with key metrics and a short demo. we can co-present with Priya if you want a customer voice.
[06:54] Priya Nandan: i'll take a 5 minute customer statement if that helps.
[06:58] Lena Ortiz: perfect.
[07:02] Arjun Rao: small gotcha: if your data contains PHI, we'll need a narrow scope and probably do a private deployment rather than hosted. please flag any PHI examples before upload.
[07:15] Luis Moreno: right — confirmed we have PHI in some records; we'll flag sensitive fields and we may opt for private deployment. can you share pricing delta for private vs hosted?
[07:26] Lena Ortiz: yes, pricing varies; for POC we can do a temporary private deployment with limited retention as an enterprise trial; we'll include a ballpark in the runbook and formal pricing in follow-up.
[07:38] Priya Nandan: final question — how do you handle model updates during the POC? if you change weights for perf, how do we compare apples-to-apples?
[07:46] Markus Chen: we'll pin model versions for benchmark runs, keep full provenance, and if we do an optimized compile/kernels run we will annotate those trials. the benchmark sheet will capture model hash, quantization flags, and runtime config so comparisons are reproducible.
[08:03] Lena Ortiz: ok let's recap action items and milestones. kickoff (today) -> access & env by 2026-06-10 -> baseline bench run week of 2026-06-22 -> mid-point review week of 2026-06-29 -> optimization & scale week of 2026-07-06 -> exec readout target week of 2026-07-13. does that calendar work?
[08:25] Carla Hughes: yes that aligns with our exec offsite.
[08:29] Priya Nandan: thanks everyone.
[08:31] Lena Ortiz: i'll send the runbook and benchmark template later today. thanks.
